title: Staged simulated failover + rollforward controller for model lifecycles
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a controller that can run deterministic simulated failovers and automated rollforward policies against canaries and shadow traffic. Improves rollback fidelity and provides a simulation mode for preflight validation.
description: Summary: Adds a Staged Simulated Failover and Rollforward Controller (SSFR Controller) to the rollout subsystem. The controller provides two complementary capabilities: (1) deterministic simulation of failover scenarios against canaries and shadow traffic to detect recoverability issues before hitting production, and (2) an automated rollforward policy that executes stepwise recovery actions when a canary has been previously rolled back but satisfies synthetic and real-world recovery conditions. Motivation: We've seen multiple incidents where rollbacks avoided immediate production impact but left systems in a state that required manual intervention to reintroduce improved models (incident write-ups: INT-903 / postmortem ENG-4078). Engineering wanted a way to validate rollback safety and to automate safe reintroduction (rollforward) when conditions recover. Design: - Simulation harness: a pluggable simulation engine that can replay sampled traffic (live-sampled shards or saved replays) through proposed rollout state transitions. The harness injects synthetic failures (latency/p95 spikes, OOM, kv-cache faults) and reports deterministic step traces. - Safety contracts: user-defined predicates (latency, error-rate, drift score, token-quality regression) that must hold for a candidate rollforward. Predicates are evaluated against both synthetic simulation outputs and live monitoring windows. - Staged actions: support for multi-step rollforward (reintroduce to 1%, 5%, 20%, full) with holdpoints, automatic gating, and a bounded backoff when metrics regress. - Conflict handling: integrates with existing rollout lease mechanism; simulation runs are non-destructive and can be triggered on PRs, canary creation, or via the Console preflight button. Implementation highlights: - New controller implementation: rollout/ssfr/controller.go — reconciler + finite-state machine to track simulated scenarios and rollforward leases. - Simulation engine: rollout/sim/engine.go + plugins for traffic sources (live-sampler, replay-store, synthetic-generator). - Policy schema bump: api/v1/rollout_policy.proto adds fields simulated_failover_config and rollforward_policy (backoff_ms, holdpoints, quality_thresholds). - Console: UI changes to add a "Run preflight simulation" button and a simulation results modal with trace visualization. - E2E tests: tests/rollout/ssfr_integration_test.go simulates deterministic fault modes and validates the rollforward decision path. Checklist: - [x] Controller reconciler + FSM implemented - [x] Policy proto schema & migration path - [x] Simulation engine + two traffic plugins - [x] Console button + results visualization (frontend + backend RPC) - [x] Unit tests for policy evaluation logic - [x] Deterministic integration tests with replay store - [x] Documentation: docs/rollouts/ssfr.md - [x] Kennel load test: 10k synthetic requests/s in canary sims Performance and safety considerations: - Simulation runs are rate-limited and sandboxed; the simulation engine uses a read-only view of live caches unless explicitly configured to use replay data. - The controller defaults to conservative rollforward thresholds (quality_thresholds defaults to 99th-percentile parity on regression metrics). - The rollforward lease duration is short (default 1h) and requires re-evaluation for further progress. Commits (high level): - feat(ssfr): core controller FSM and reconciliation loop - feat(sim): simulation engine and live-sampler plugin - feat(api): rollout_policy.proto schema additions + migration helpers - feat(console): preflight simulation endpoint and frontend modal - test(ssfr): integration + unit test coverage - docs(rollouts): ssfr user guide and runbook Changed areas/files (high level): - rollout/controller/ssfr_controller.go (new) - rollout/sim/engine.go, rollout/sim/plugins/live_sampler.go, rollout/sim/plugins/replay_store.go - api/v1/rollout_policy.proto (schema bump) - console/src/components/SimulationModal.tsx, console/src/routes/rolloutDetail.tsx - tests/rollout/ssfr_integration_test.go - docs/rollouts/ssfr.md - scripts/migrate-rollout-policy.sh Example snippets: - Policy example (proto-compact): simulated_failover_config { inject_latency_ms: 200 fail_rate_pct: 0.5 } rollforward_policy { holdpoints: [1,5,20] quality_thresholds { drift_score_max: 0.02 latency_p95_max_ms: 250 } } - Simulation run command (CLI): rwctl rollout simulate --policy-id=pol_123 --replay=2026-02-14/sha256:abcd --inject=latency:200ms Review conversation (threads condensed into a single narrative): - Daniel Kim (review): "High-level: really powerful. Please make the simulation engine opt-in for hosted tenants by default; we can't allow accidental replay of PII. Also add a flag to enforce read-only cache access." — Asha replied: "Done, engine defaults to replay-store: off. Added explicit replay.allow_pii boolean and documentation note." - Sven Müller (review): "FSM looks good, but I'm worried about lease explosion. Can we add a global rate limiter and a max-concurrent-simulations config?" — Asha: "Added controller-level semaphore and metrics rollout.ssfr.concurrent_simulations with config 'max_simulations' in cluster config." - Priya Nair (QA): "Integration test is flaky in CI (race on replay-store initialization)." — Asha: "Fixed race by introducing explicit store readiness check and added a retry/backoff in test harness." CI and rollout to prod: - Initial CI run: unit tests + linters passed; integration failed due to replay-store race (fixed in subsequent commit). - Final CI run: all checks green (unit/integration/e2e/flaky retries). - Canary rollout: rolled to internal staging cluster first (passed), then gradual rollout to dedicated canaries. - Merge: squash merge after approvals. Merge notes: merged by Sven Müller via squash on 2026-03-02. Post-merge actions: - ops: schedule a canary policy migration with database migration script (scripts/migrate-rollout-policy.sh). - infra: add default max_simulations=3 cluster config to prevent runaway simulations. - docs: team runbook updated with SSFR playbook and incident remediation steps. Known limitations & follow-ups: - Current simulation plugins do not cover GPU OOM patterns — follow-up ENG-4287. - Replay store can be large; added TTL but long-term retention policy planned (ENG-4299). - UI improvements: add diff view between simulated vs live metrics (future work). Related work: ENG-4129 (preflight validation initiative), ENG-4172 (rollout lease improvements), INT-903 postmortem. Why unique: Unlike previous rollout PRs this one focuses on preflight simulation + automated rollforward (not just rollback) and bridges replayed/simulated failure modes with live gating logic so teams can both validate and recover models with reduced manual steps. If you want to run the simulation locally: see docs/rollouts/ssfr.md (section: developer quickstart).
ci_and_rollout_summary: Initial CI run: unit tests + linters passed; integration failed due to replay-store race (fixed). Final CI run: all checks green. Canary rollout staged then gradual to dedicated canaries. Squash merged by Sven Müller on 2026-03-02.
